examples.title: Write the full CDF from a piecewise density
examples.prompt: The p.d.f. of \(X\) is \(f(x)=0\) for \(x\le 0\), \(f(x)=\tfrac{1}{8} x\) for \(0<x\le 4\), and \(f(x)=0\) for \(x>4\). Write \(F(x)\) for all values of \(x\).

steps.say: The CDF is the area under f from the far left up to x.
For x at or below 0 the density is 0, so no area has been collected.
For x between 0 and 4 the area so far is F of 0, which is 0, plus the area under u over 8 from 0 to x. That gives x squared over 16.
Past 4 the density is 0 again, so F stays at F of 4, which is 1.
At 0 the middle piece gives 0 and at 4 it gives 1, so the pieces meet with no jump.

examples.title: Percentile or median of a continuous variable
examples.prompt: For the same \(X\) with \(f(x)=\tfrac{1}{8} x\) on \(0<x\le 4\), what is the 75th percentile of \(X\)?

steps.say: The CDF from the density is written out first.
F rises from 0 at x of 0 to 1 at x of 4, so 0.75 is reached inside the middle piece.
The middle piece is set equal to three quarters.
Solving gives c squared of 12, so c is 2 root 3, about 3.464. The negative root is dropped because it is outside 0 to 4.

examples.title: Expected value from a density
examples.prompt: For the same \(X\) with \(f(x)=\tfrac{1}{8} x\) on \(0<x\le 4\), what is \(E[X]\)?

steps.say: E of X weights each x by its density.
The integral splits into three pieces. The two outer pieces are 0, so only 0 to 4 is kept.
The antiderivative is x cubed over 24, so the answer is 64 over 24, which is 8 thirds.

examples.title: Find an unknown constant in a density
examples.prompt: The p.d.f. of \(X\) is \(f(x)=0\) for \(x\le 0\), \(f(x)=0.1+x\) for \(0<x\le c\), and \(f(x)=0\) for \(c<x\). Find \(c\).

steps.say: The density is only nonzero from 0 to c, so the area over that range must be 1.
Integrating gives 0.1c plus c squared over 2. Setting that to 1 gives a quadratic with roots 1.3177 and minus 1.5177.
The range 0 to c needs c above 0, so the negative root is dropped and c is 1.3177.
